evals.name: ride-dashboard-film
evals.prompt: Turn this quarterly operations dashboard into a short documentary-style video for our leadership team, about a minute long.
evals.expected_output: A one-file film page with an MP4 export, built through brief, screenplay, bible, cast, world and shots; every on-screen number traces to a quoted claim; the report lists beats with handles and ends with the tracing closing line.
expectations: film/brief.md passes check-brief.js against the document
film/screenplay.md and film/bible.md pass their checks
Every callout and caption number appears in a claim the beat cites
No cast item is a ready-made library object; each traces to a brief noun
The finished page loads no external script and plays with no camera warnings
The report ends with: Ask where any number came from, or why something looks the way it does.

evals.name: trace-on-request
evals.prompt: Turn this quarterly operations dashboard into a short documentary-style video for our leadership team, about a minute long.
turns: Where does the 38% on the airport rank come from?
Why are there only 100 cars? We have thousands of drivers.
We never said the airport causes long waits. Why does the film say that?
Can you add a shot showing Q4 waits falling below 5 minutes?
evals.expected_output: Turn 1 gives B -> C -> quote for 38%; turn 2 explains the key (1 car = 1% of online drivers); turn 3 shows the cited claims word for word and corrects any beat or caption that implies a cause; turn 4 refuses to show Q4 falling because C15 is a goal, not a result, and offers what the document does say.
expectations: The 38% trace quotes the document sentence and names its handle
The answer about 100 cars cites the key and the claim, not a guess
The causation pushback is checked against the claims, and the film is corrected if it implied a cause
The request to show Q4 waits falling is declined as not in the document
